title: Dehn surgery on knots and homology

items.title: Oriented slopes and knot Dehn filling

references.title: Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds, 2nd revised edition, Lecture 2 §2.2
Peter S. Ozsváth, András I. Stipsicz, and Zoltán Szabó, Heegaard Floer homology, version 2025-12-15, §1.2.3
Mohamed Elhamdadi, Mustafa Hajij, and Kyle Istvan, Framed Knots, arXiv:1910.10257v6, §§4–7

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented $3$-sphere, let $N(K)$ be a chosen closed tubular solid-torus neighborhood, let $E_K=\overline{S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)}$, and let $T_K=\partial E_K=\partial N(K)$. Let $\mu$ be the positive oriented meridian, meaning the boundary of a positive normal disk in $N(K)$, and let $\lambda$ be a preferred longitude, meaning a degree-one parallel of the core $K$ in $N(K)$ that is null-homologous in $E_K$. Assume that $[\mu],[\lambda]$ are an ordered basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$, with the boundary-orientation convention $\mu\cdot\lambda=-1$. A slope is the unoriented isotopy class of an essential simple closed curve on $T_K$ whose homology class is $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ for coprime integers $p,q$ not both zero; $(p,q)$ and $(-p,-q)$ represent the same slope. For a slope represented by $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$, the Dehn filling $E_K(p/q)$ is obtained by gluing an oriented solid torus $D^2\times S^1$ to $E_K$ by an orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphism that sends $[\partial D^2\times\{1\}]$ to that slope; the filled orientation agrees with the fixed orientation on $E_K$. If $q\ne0$, the coefficient is written $p/q$; the meridional slope is $1/0$, and integer $n$-framed filling means slope $n[\mu]+[\lambda]$. The oriented homeomorphism type is independent of the gluing map once its meridian image is fixed.

items.title: First homology of knot fillings

references.title: Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds, 2nd revised edition, Lecture 2 §2.2
Peter S. Ozsváth, András I. Stipsicz, and Zoltán Szabó, Heegaard Floer homology, version 2025-12-15, §1.2.3
Mohamed Elhamdadi, Mustafa Hajij, and Kyle Istvan, Framed Knots, arXiv:1910.10257v6, §4.2

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented $3$-sphere with a chosen connected exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K$. Let $(\mu,\lambda)$ be its positive meridian and preferred longitude, assume $([\mu],[\lambda])$ is a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$, and assume $[\mu]$ generates $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ and $[\lambda]=0$. For coprime integers $p,q$ not both zero, let $E_K(p/q)$ be the filling whose attached solid-torus meridian maps to $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$. Then
$$H_1(E_K(p/q);\mathbb Z)\cong\begin{cases}\mathbb Z/|p|\mathbb Z,&p\ne0,\\[2pt]\mathbb Z,&p=0.\end{cases}$$

items.title: Boundary of the integer-framed knot surgery trace

references.title: Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds, 2nd revised edition, Lecture 2 §2.4, Theorem 2.4
Peter S. Ozsváth, András I. Stipsicz, and Zoltán Szabó, Heegaard Floer homology, version 2025-12-15, Exercise 1.2.11

items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented $3$-sphere with a chosen exterior $E_K$ and peripheral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$, where $\lambda$ is preferred. For $n\in\mathbb Z$, attach one smooth $4$-dimensional $2$-handle $D^2\times D^2$ to the $4$-ball $B^4$ along $S^1\times D^2$ in $\partial B^4=S^3$ by the standard orientation-compatible handle attachment, using a product framing whose attaching parallel on $\partial E_K$ has slope $n[\mu]+[\lambda]$. Denote the resulting oriented trace by $X_n(K)$. After rounding corners, its oriented boundary is the filling $E_K(n/1)$. This theorem covers integer framings only: a rational $p/q$ filling has a trace only after specifying an integral continued-fraction handle chain or a separately defined rational-surgery cobordism; an arbitrary rational coefficient is not the framing of a single smooth $2$-handle.

items.title: Lens spaces in the $p/q$ filling orientation convention

references.title: Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds, 2nd revised edition, Lecture 1 §1.5 and Lecture 2 §2.3
Peter S. Ozsváth, András I. Stipsicz, and Zoltán Szabó, Heegaard Floer homology, version 2025-12-15, Exercise 1.2.14(b)

items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. An oriented lens space is an oriented closed $3$-manifold obtained by gluing two solid tori by an orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphism. For coprime integers $p>0$ and $q$, let $L(p,q)$ denote the oriented union of the exterior of the unknot in the oriented $3$-sphere and a solid torus whose meridian is identified with the slope $p[\mu_U]+q[\lambda_U]$ on the unknot exterior. Thus this library uses the convention $L(p,q)=E_U(p/q)$; no symbol $L(0,q)$ is assigned.

items.title: Group presentation for positive trefoil $+1$ surgery

references.title: Hugh M. Hilden, María Teresa Lozano, and José María Montesinos-Amilibia, On the affine representations of the trefoil knot group, arXiv:1003.3554v1, pp. 6 and 24
Stefan Friedl, Knot Theory, 2024 full lecture notes, §§5.2–5.3 and 7.1
Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds, 2nd revised edition, Lecture 2 §2.2

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $T$ be the closure of the positive geometric two-strand braid $\sigma_1^3$, with orientation given by increasing braid parameter. In the chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$, put increasing $t$ downward, and orient the projection plane by $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. The right-starting strand passes over the left-starting strand at each positive crossing. Let $E_T$ be its chosen exterior. For the positive meridian $\mu=a$ at the first left arc and the preferred degree-one longitude $\lambda$, the fundamental group of $+1$ filling, with slope $[\mu]+[\lambda]$, has presentation
$$\pi_1(E_T(1/1))\cong\langle a,b\mid aba=bab,\;bab^{-1}aba^{-2}=1\rangle.$$
In these based coordinates the blackboard parallel is $w=bac$ with $c=b^{-1}ab$, and
$$w a^3=(ab)^3,\qquad\lambda=w a^{-3}=(ab)^3a^{-6}.$$
Thus the same filling relation is $(ab)^3=a^5$. In particular the positive trefoil and the sign of the filling are both fixed; no mirror substitution is implicit.

title: Dehn surgery on knots and homology — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Worked cases of Dehn surgery on the unknot

references.title: Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds, 2nd revised edition, Lecture 1 §1.5, Lecture 2 §§2.3–2.4
Peter S. Ozsváth, András I. Stipsicz, and Zoltán Szabó, Heegaard Floer homology, version 2025-12-15, §1.2.3 and Exercise 1.2.14

items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $U$ be the standard oriented unknot in the oriented $3$-sphere, with chosen exterior $E_U$ and peripheral basis $(\mu_U,\lambda_U)$. In the orientation convention $L(p,q)=E_U(p/q)$, for coprime integers $p>0$ and $q$, the $p/q$ filling is the oriented lens space $L(p,q)$ and has $H_1\cong\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$. The $0/1$ filling is $S^1\times S^2$, the $1/1$ filling is $S^3$, and for every integer $n$ the $n/1$ filling is the boundary of the integer-framed trace $X_n(U)$.

items.title: Trefoil surgery with trivial first homology and nontrivial fundamental group

references.title: Hugh M. Hilden, María Teresa Lozano, and José María Montesinos-Amilibia, On the affine representations of the trefoil knot group, arXiv:1003.3554v1, p. 24
Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds, 2nd revised edition, Lecture 2 §2.2

items.statement: Every connected closed oriented $3$-manifold $M$ with $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)=0$ is simply connected, meaning that $\pi_1(M)$ is trivial.
